description: Runnable templates and recipes for Cartesia: Sonic text to speech, Ink speech to text and Managed Agents voice agents in Next.js, Node, Python and Expo.
rules: Use model_id sonic-3.6 for text to speech. Its pinned snapshot is sonic-3.6-2026-08-27. Every other Sonic model id is sunset, scheduled for sunset on 2026-10-20, or a deprecated alias.
Use ink-2 for streaming speech to text with turn detection (/stt/turns/websocket; en, es, fr, hi, ja). Use ink-whisper for file transcription; ink-2 does not work on the batch endpoint.
The API version header is Cartesia-Version: 2026-08-14. The SDKs send it, so do not override it. Browser WebSockets pass ?cartesia_version= instead.
Use the official SDKs: @cartesia/cartesia-js 4.x for TypeScript and cartesia 4.x for Python. The Python client does not read CARTESIA_API_KEY itself; pass api_key=os.environ["CARTESIA_API_KEY"].

Never send CARTESIA_API_KEY to a browser or mobile bundle. A server route mints client.accessToken.create({ grants, expires_in: 60 }) with the narrowest grants (agent, tts or stt) and the browser uses that token.
Managed Agents WebSocket: wss://api.cartesia.ai/v1/agents/websocket/{agent_id}, opened with an access token that has the agent grant. Client tool results must be under 4096 bytes.
Return fixed error messages from routes. Do not forward SDK error text or upstream response bodies to the client.

To start a new app, clone a template: pnpm dlx create-next-app --example https://github.com/cartesia-ai/cookbook/tree/main/examples/<slug> (Next.js) or pnpm dlx degit cartesia-ai/cookbook/examples/<slug>.
